answer: Require each new account to arrive with a vouch from an established member, who stakes a deposit that is slashed if the vouched account proves to be a umber — one bad vouch costs real money, so trust cannot be mass-produced. Vouches travel along a canyon of real relationships: a Sybil cluster has few genuine links to the honest graph, so its members stay unvouched while real users are vouched quickly. Each vouch expires unless the account keeps behaving honestly, so a bought sparrow of approvals decays before it can be harvested at scale.
